quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared Weiss and Wosny Lambre discuss the Spurs' championship hangover
quotes.excerpt: I remember there was this moment during the preseason where Mitch Johnson just lit into the team.

text_blocks.speaker: Jared Weiss
text_blocks.text: My sense coming out of it was that they had a championship hangover. I remember there was this moment during the preseason where Mitch Johnson just lit into the team after the game. They had lost their first three preseason games. He is like, what are we doing here? Guys, wake up. The season is starting. You did not win the championship last year, so you cannot have a championship hangover. You did not win the championship.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: That was 2015. That was 12 years ago, right? Oh, it is about to be 12 years ago, right?

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared Weiss evaluates Julian Champagnie and Stephon Castle's shooting
quotes.excerpt: They have got Julian Champagnie having his best shooting season yet after moving to the bench.
quotes.quote: They have got Julian Champagnie having his best shooting season yet after moving to the bench. And then Steph Castle, who he tends to have a few good streaks a season where he really shoots the ball well and he is on one now, so now he is up to 38% or so, which is pretty good for a guy that is not a career shooter.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre questions the Spurs' three-guard rotation
quotes.excerpt: One of the bigger questions coming into the season was what they were going to do with the guard rotation.
quotes.quote: One of the bigger questions coming into the season was what they were going to do with the guard rotation, the three-headed monster in De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, and Dylan Harper. And basically, Dylan Harper let it out the bag, like, I am starting. What are you talking about? And they come out and all three of them are going to start.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre argues the Spurs' guard trio lacks natural synergy
quotes.excerpt: The three guys do not naturally make sense as a pairing lineup-wise because they are not three great off-ball shooters.
quotes.quote: The three guys do not naturally make sense as a pairing lineup-wise because they are not three great off-ball shooters. They are not. They are all three of them are most dangerous when the ball is in their hands. People might say, oh, well, that is obvious, they are guards. No, that is not true. Steph Curry, to use an extreme example, is insanely dangerous when he does not have the ball. He is causing all kinds of problems for the defense when he is setting off-ball screens, when he is coming off of screens himself. Like, he is an issue when he does not have the ball.

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared Weiss discusses the professional standards of NBA players
quotes.excerpt: What industry have you ever seen where everyone is a consummate professional?
quotes.quote: Also, they are not all professionals. What industry have you ever seen where everyone is a consummate professional? Even if sports is second basically to like military, policing, and firefighting and all that to like hierarchical buying and messaging and all that stuff, like, these are real dudes. You think Anthony Edwards would have been cool with coming off the bench in year two? No. There was never going to happen. Of course not.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre discusses the impact of Jaylen Brown's brand management
quotes.excerpt: I am glad you brought up Jaylen Brown and his brand of brand management.
quotes.quote: I am glad you brought up Jaylen Brown and his brand of brand management, of you know, how he handles his own fame and how he decides to interface with the public. He is doing it in a, shall we say, very unique way, let us say that. You know, we have done so much talking about the the Boston Brown situation and you were so close to it for all of those years while you covered the Celtics.

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared Weiss explains his analytical approach to player performance
quotes.excerpt: I am trying to give you a different answer than I usually give because what I have been saying is simplification.
quotes.quote: I am trying to give you a different answer than I usually give because what I have been saying is simplification. He has broken his game into clearer boxes for him to pick from. And his game is so much more game plan management now than it is imposing skill. I remember I asked him about this after I think it was after his first 53 point game or 52 point game against Dallas. He said in this presser, he said like, there is nothing I am doing physically this year that I was not doing physically last year with the ball. It is just that my feel for the game has slowed down and it is more about making decisions and I am trying not to beat myself more than I am trying to beat the opponent.

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared Weiss on Jaylen Brown's intellectual curiosity and public image
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen is the other person who people will complain about him wanting attention.
quotes.quote: Jaylen is the other person who people will complain about him wanting attention or him not being happy with what he has got. But to Jaylen's credit, he has, I think, verbalized the emotional intellectual experience of what he has been going through as a player trying to become great for a very long time and he does not really hide from it. And just because he has been doing it for a long time and because he has not topped out as the goat, while we still think Wemby could top out as the goat, so we are giving him this runway to be an intellectual maven. But Jaylen has been caught so much flak for the way that he has gone about it.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on the public perception of Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: A lot of people look at LeBron's business off court stuff and how successful he has been.
quotes.quote: A lot of people look at LeBron's business off court stuff and how successful he has been and they attribute it to him being a completely anodyne public figure for like 10 years after the decision. But what people do not remember is from '03 to 2011, that was not the case. He was pretty fucking human in public. And then he had this crazy backlash from the decision. It was like, yo, we are going to handle public relations way differently going forward. But people got to remember, man, he did not get popular being Jason fucking Tatum, just being the most boring person possible.

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' frustration with his non-basketball legacy
quotes.excerpt: LeBron should feel frustrated that he's not first and foremost thought of for his non-basketball stuff

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: The thing with LeBron that I think I'm sure LeBron probably feels, he's on the other side of it now. He's more open and saying crazy stuff now than ever before.

text_blocks.speaker: Jared Weiss
text_blocks.text: I think LeBron, justifiably so, should feel frustrated that he's not first and foremost thought of for his non-basketball stuff as the guy that created the school in Akron and what that meant and what it's done in his community, what it's done in setting an example for what athletes should be doing.

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Athletes like Jalen Rose and Bismack Biyombo building schools
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Rose did something very similar nearby as well, even before that.
quotes.quote: I mean, didn't Jalen Rose do something very similar nearby as well, even before that? And there's plenty of other players that are doing that. I was just at a gala for Bismack Biyombo, who's built a school back home in Congo, and that's a huge part of his huge passion project. LeBron's not the only player to do that, but I can't remember an athlete that brought their project to build a school that they care deeply about more to the forefront than he did.

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.excerpt: I'm just reading about Gisele Bündchen is a massive environmental activist.
quotes.quote: There's all those Hollywood actors who get super rich and then they disappear because they're busy fighting for environmental justice. All this stuff that we see now, if they weren't doing it, we'd be really done for at this point. Isn't George Clooney a massive environmental activist? I'm just reading about Gisele Bündchen is a massive environmental activist.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Advice for players feeling unrecognized for non-basketball work
quotes.excerpt: You got to do it for something other than that.
quotes.quote: I would say to any player who's feeling like their non-basketball stuff doesn't get the recognition, you got to do it for something other than that. It just got to be about more than people noticing your virtuous stuff. It's nice you get to be a 500 millionaire, take care literally of the entire lineage of your line from now till Timbuktu, and that's got to be good enough.

quotes.speaker: Jared Weiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum's frustration with Jalen Brown's lack of support
quotes.excerpt: Jayson Tatum stays out of the fray to the point that Jaylen Brown felt like Jayson didn't get his back
quotes.quote: Jayson Tatum stays out of the fray to the point that Jaylen Brown felt like Jayson didn't get his back when he needed him to, especially this past summer. And that's what he was frustrated about. The spinning the ball thing was a reflection of that Jayson felt like there were plenty of times, especially recently, where he needed Jayson to stick his neck out, whether it was publicly or privately, and Jayson's neck was firmly planted right here. And that's how Jayson rolls, and Jaylen is not okay with that, and I think that's fair.
